what: Religious mendicants not rare; fifteen orders known but only Dasnami and Barapanthi numerically important; the Dasnami are "an order of the Gosains"; many have adopted agriculture and marriage
quote: Fifteen different orders are known, but the Dasnami and the Barapanthi alone are numerically important The former are an order of the Gosains.

what: Barapanthi (Kanphata Jogi order) named as second numerically important order of mendicants (identification as Jogi is from context of Nath/Barapanthi only; not glossed in text)
quote: the Dasnami and the Barapanthi alone are numerically important

what: Many members of the religious fraternities have taken to agriculture and marriage, indistinguishable from hillmen except in dress
quote: Many members of the roligious fraternities have now adopted agriculture and marriage and except in certain peculiarities of thoir dress are not distinguished from ordinary hillmen.

what: Sankara Acharya expelled corrupt Buddhism from Kumaon and re-established Kedarnath, Badrinath and Joshimath temples; founded a temple at Joshimath to Vishnu as Basdeo and another at Badrinath
quote: the great reformer Sankara Acharya expelled from Kumaon : or rather ... re-established the famous temples at Kedarnath, Badrinath and Joshimath.

what: Khasiyas did not profess the Vedantic religion until arrival of Sankara Acharya
quote: they would appear in the first place not to have professed the V edantic religion until the arrival of Sankara Acharya.

what: From Dwarahat westward the principal temples are ascribed to Sankara Acharya; Badrinath temple at Dwarahat controlled by the Rawal of Badrinath in Garhwal
quote: From Dwarahat westward, all the principal temples are ascribed to Sankara Acharya

place: Aijnath (Aijnath/Baijnath?), patti Bichla Katyur, pargana Danpur
what: Colony of Gosains with burial of dead in small temple-like tombs around their place of worship (Saiva; samadhi practice)
quote: A colony of Gosains are established here, who observe the custom of burying their dead in small temple-like tombs around the building in which they worship.

place: Pinnath (Pinakeswar), patti Palla Borakan, pargana Barahmandal
what: Colony of Gosains; their mahants buried nearby with domed tombs and miniature linga; hold copper-plate grants of land to Siva as Pinakeswar from Udyot Chand (1691 AD/1613 samvat) and Baz Bahadur Chand (1654)
quote: A colony of Gosains resides here and a number of their mahants lie buried close by, each with a small dome over his remains surmounted by a miniature ling.

what: Gosains hold metal-plate land grants from Chand Rajas (1613 sam. and 1654 AD)
quote: The Gosains possess a grant engraved in metal conferring lauds on Siva as Pinakeswar, executed by Udyot Chand, Raja of Kumaon, in 1613 samvat

what: Mohan Singh with a band of "religious mendicants called Nagas" made an unsuccessful attempt on Almora (c.1779-88)
quote: Singh with the assistance of a band of religious mendicants called Nagas, made another unsuccessful attempt upon Almora.

what: Sakti Gosain, Nil Gosain, Piru Gosain, Himmat Gosain: Gosain as title/name of Chand princes and officers; not an order
quote: ably assisted by his blind son Sakti Gosain he introduced many sensible reforms

what: Raj family of Rajwar: eldest son called Lala, younger son Gosain (title of cadet, not ascetic)
quote: the eldest son is called Lala and the younger Gosain.
